biography:
Brent Millage, a name synonymous with both brilliance and bewildering inconsistency, hails from the quaint Cotswolds village of Bourton-on-the-Water. His racing journey began not on a meticulously groomed track, but on the muddy fields of his family's farm, tearing around on a battered quad bike he affectionately nicknamed 'The Beast.' It was during one particularly soggy harvest that Brent, then just 16, executed a daring overtake on his uncle's tractor, a move that cemented his passion for speed and competition. He transitioned into karting, displaying raw talent but struggling with the discipline required for consistent results. 

His career reached a turning point when he joined Caterham Superlight. While flashes of brilliance earned him podium finishes, frustrating incidents of poor judgment, like spinning out while leading at Brands Hatch in 2021, became a recurring theme. Despite the rollercoaster of emotions, Millage's undeniable speed and unwavering determination have kept him in the sport, fueled by a burning desire to finally unlock his full potential. He is seen as a driver who will win or crash trying.

Now at 32, and arguably in his peak physical condition, Brent faces an uphill battle to redeem himself. His recent performance in the Caterham Superlight series is under scrutiny, with some critics suggesting his inconsistent nature may be impossible to overcome. Yet, his loyal fans, who affectionately call him 'The Wild Hare,' cling to the hope that he will finally harness his raw talent and deliver the championship-winning performance he has always threatened.
drivingStyle: Millage's driving style is best described as 'seat-of-the-pants.' He's an instinctive racer, relying on feel and reaction rather than meticulous data analysis. He attacks corners aggressively, often pushing the limits of grip to gain an advantage. While this approach can lead to spectacular overtakes, it also makes him prone to errors, especially in wet conditions where his lack of finesse is amplified. Tire management is not his forte; he often burns through rubber in the early stages of a race, leaving him vulnerable in the closing laps. Under pressure, Millage tends to become even more erratic, either pulling off miraculous feats or succumbing to unforced errors.

rivalries.reason: A bitter rivalry sparked in their karting days, Dubois, a master of consistency, often capitalized on Millage's mistakes, leading to several heated on-track battles and off-track exchanges.

Tanaka, a calculated and precise driver, represents everything Millage is not. Their contrasting styles often clash on the track, with Millage viewing Tanaka as overly cautious and Tanaka seeing Millage as reckless.

Both talented drivers in the Caterham Superlight, Silva and Millage have had multiple incidents of contact while jockeying for position. Silva accuses Millage of overly aggressive moves, while Millage claims Silva blocks unfairly.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of argyle socks for every race, despite them being heavily worn.
Has a pre-race ritual of eating exactly three jelly babies, each a different color.
Insists on personally polishing his helmet visor before every session, believing it improves his visibility, even at night.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about being perfect, it's about being brave enough to make mistakes and still push harder."
careerHighlight: Winning the wet race at Silverstone in 2019, where he demonstrated incredible car control and overtook three cars in the final lap to snatch victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the last lap of the Brands Hatch race in 2021 due to over exuberance, costing him valuable championship points.
